purpose: Consolidated work tracker for the Luzon delivery phase. This is not a species checklist, complete waterbody inventory, release manifest, or claim of biological absence.

limitations: The national registry supplies the pinned region, province, and separately represented independent-city baseline; its lower-level locality rows are out of scope. CALABARZON's working municipality/city name-code denominator is separately recorded in national/reviews/calabarzon-administrative-denominator-reconciliation-20261117.json; it contains no boundary geometry.
MIMAROPA is included in the Luzon delivery phase by project convention; administrative membership, island group, drainage basin, and marine study area remain separate relationships.

baselineReviewedDefinition: Use the completion gates in docs/PHILIPPINES_SPECIES_EXPANSION_PLAN.md section 3. A region is baseline-reviewed only after its complete administrative and source-derived waterbody scope is reconciled, source searches and candidate decisions are accounted for, evidence and reuse checks pass, every waterbody has an explicit coverage result, and counts reconcile.

completionGates.requirement: Account for all current provinces, applicable NCR units, independent cities, and needed lower-level locality crosswalks in the pinned administrative snapshot.
Reconcile source-derived marine, brackish, and inland waters, including rivers, tributaries, streams, natural lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, ponds, and islands where applicable.
Process each agreed source/search or record the access, rights, or evidence gap with attempted alternatives and a follow-up owner.
Give each snapshot candidate an evidence-backed admit, exclude, or hold decision. A hold is triage, not coverage.
Validate taxon identity, locality, date, provenance, item and dataset reuse terms, and citation before public projection.
Show a coverage result per inventoried waterbody; no usable record is a visible gap, never a species-absence claim.
Reconcile raw, normalized, mirrored, admitted, excluded, and held counts and list remaining gaps in each regional manifest.

regions.name: Region IV-A (CALABARZON)

appFacingResearchProjection.scope: Attributed, historical Palico-Lian survey-table assertions with unknown observation date; not a current checklist, abundance estimate, or complete regional baseline.

openWork: Reconcile the selected 164 waterbody leads and new source-derived additions against the 120-municipality/22-city locality denominator, including islands, shared waters, and freshwater, brackish, and marine lanes; this locality denominator is not a waterbody inventory.
Keep source-specific survey assertions distinct from the scope file's waterbody/public-admission counters when reconciling CALABARZON counts.

Keep Manila Bay shared with NCR and Central Luzon under one canonical waterbody identity. The 19 November National Museum crosswalk matched all 524 OBIS rows to GBIF occurrence IDs and four of seven Cavite administrative-text candidates; it adds no capture-site or Cavite-water assignment. Reconcile other sources and localities separately; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.
Keep the three historical CAS Santa Cruz River records held from public projection and redistributed packages until the Academy clarifies its no-redistribution terms versus GBIF CC0 metadata.
Keep the Laguna Lakeshore Road Network EIS as a West Bay retrieval lead; its mixed 2014/2020 fish summaries lack a verified adult-fish site/date/voucher crosswalk and item-specific reuse approval.
Use independently reusable, site-resolved sources for other CALABARZON inland waters while Taal CAS redistribution terms and Dryad file access remain unresolved.
Reconcile the wetlands denominator, unnamed river/wetland counts, and modeled stream identities before claiming complete coverage.

After eight 19 November CALABARZON source-backed locality batches, the selected 164-lead scope has 80 city/municipality-linked leads, 80 province-only leads, and 4 without any locality code; represented CALABARZON coverage is 15/22 city codes and 49/120 municipality codes. BMB locality contexts include six San Pablo lakes, Yellow/Tadlac/Caliraya, three Laguna cities, three Rizal municipalities, and the separately reviewed NCR localities around one shared Laguna de Bay identity, Tanza for the Tres Cruzes candidate, Rodriguez for Wawa Dam, Cavinti for the NPC-reported Lumot Lake event locality, and the 14-LGU Taal Lake planning cluster; a working Mojicap/Mohicap alias for the San Pablo City lead is supported by LLDA lists. Retain the Tres Cruzes class/identity hold, Wawa boundaries/access limitations, Lumot reservoir extent/identity caveat, and distinguish the Taal planning cluster and all source-described localities from lake geometry. Keep scopeFrozen=false.

The 17 November exact GBIF name/alias screen returned two 1941 CAS preserved-specimen candidates for waterBody=Bay River; both remain held because locality is “3 km from Laguna de Bay” with 1,743 m uncertainty. Thirteen other exact-field searches returned zero and do not establish absence.

The cross-region 2022 PAREX EIS labels station FWE 6 as Taytay, Rizal. Keep that one-day fish-survey station separate from Laguna de Bay fish evidence and hold its locality-to-waterbody identity until independently crosswalked.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station identity is not crosswalked, and the NFRDI article gives conflicting approximate spacing in its abstract and methods. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

Dryad’s public dataset metadata API now returns HTTP 200 for the 2011 Taal barcode record, but version/file-list API requests timed out and the ordinary SpecimenData.xlsx link returned 403. Dryad documents an API token for file downloads; no authenticated route was used, so the spreadsheet, voucher/locality rows, and photos remain uninspected. Keep searching independent CALABARZON inland sources; see national/reviews/calabarzon-taal-aquilino-dryad-api-access-refresh-20261119.json.

regions.name: National Capital Region (NCR)
openWork: The 17-unit NCR administrative denominator matches PSA's rendered 16-city and one-municipality tables, and PSA's revision notices support its continuity through Q3 2026; the linked workbook itself remains unparsed. The historical 18-item checkpoint is a mixed set of waterway, shared-water, reservoir, watershed, wetland-park, and habitat contexts, not 18 validated waterbodies. The 2025 DENR-NCR Gawad Taga-Ilog review crosswalks 12 selected nominations to 12 reported city/municipality codes. Follow-ups corroborate the BMB Jamboree Lake name/locality and identify a BMB NAPWC pond alias candidate plus a named OSM polygon. The polygon is community mapped; the official shoreline, BMB-to-OSM crosswalk, and conflicting 3.39 ha versus approximate 4.0 ha area descriptions remain unresolved. No current access or fish claim is established. Continue broader freshwater, brackish, marine, and habitat source searches.

Extend the source-named inventory and bounded occurrence screens across freshwater, brackish, and marine contexts without treating selected program nominations or candidate hits as a complete inventory or validated capture sites.

Keep Pasig-Marikina reaches, tidal/brackish waters, Manila Bay, and Laguna de Bay connections distinct. The 19 November crosswalk found the 65 National Museum rows from the NCR administrative query among the GBIF bounding-box records and none in the 524-row OBIS result; this is feed/query coverage, not a Manila Bay or NCR-water assignment. Reconcile other shared-bay sources with L1 and L3; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

The DENR-NCR report remains a system-scope and narrative lead without fish-by-site rows; the Marikina preprint remains an eight-taxon research crosswalk. La Mesa Reservoir has five historical host-fish candidates from a 1989-1990 parasite study (234 examined across taxa), not an abundance estimate; hold its Therapon date conflict and Arius/Netuma identity concern. Lopez (1992) is identified through a 2001 secondary citation, but the original proceedings and its methods, dates, denominators, and vouchers remain unverified. Continue freshwater, brackish, and marine source searches and reconcile all candidates against the incomplete waterbody scope.

The 2015 BMB guidebook and 2016 bulletin remain vernacular historical fish leads without traceable fish-survey methods. Five exact-text CoL XR searches returned zero. A bounded GBIF spatial search found one iNaturalist Channa striata observation inside the community-mapped OSM lagoon ring, but its 8 m uncertainty exceeds the approximately 7 m point-to-edge distance; GBIF also flags TAXON_ID_NOT_FOUND and the record has no waterBody/locality. Keep it unassigned and research-only. A secondary blog lists binomials without survey provenance; a peer-reviewed NAPWC microcrustacean study is not fish evidence. Seek a directly verifiable fish survey and review current protected-area access separately.

The 2022 PAREX Revised EIS adds a one-day, six-station fish-survey lead along the Pasig corridor, with FWE 6 labeled Taytay, Rizal. Its 14-species narrative conflicts with the 13-binomial station matrix, and Table 2-20 differs from Table 2-19. A 19 November 2026 locality crosswalk found an OSM reverse-geocoder road label in Pasig while the official MRT4 EIS lists several Taytay waterway names without linking any to the PAREX point; the station waterbody remains unresolved. Keep all names and coordinates research-only pending table reconciliation, voucher evidence, a source-matched locality link, and item-specific reuse review.

The 2019 Makati Public Rail EIS states that fish sampling at its five Pasig freshwater-ecology stations was unsuccessful; those coordinates are for plankton/benthos context, not fish occurrences. Its separate eight-name reported-fish table mixes one informal observation, two secondary citations, washout context, and unsourced rows. Keep all names research-only and continue NCR freshwater/brackish/marine source searches.

The 2018 New Manila Reclamation EIS and its companion hearing report describe the same three-station Pasig survey and repeat a six-brackishwater-species summary dominated by 'Tilapia'. The hearing-report photos are captioned only with ambiguous common names ('knife fish' and 'janitor fish'); no scientific identities or table rows were recovered. Direct PDF requests returned 403, and no taxa, photos, coordinates, occurrences, or safety claims were added. See national/reviews/ncr-new-manila-reclamation-pasig-hearing-followup-20261119.json.

The cited Orozco & Zafaralla (2012) chapter is explicitly about Estero de San Miguel and Estero de Quiapo; its abstract reports Rasbora maculata and Anabas testudineus among four fish taxa, without species-to-station assignments. A related 2008 DLSU article describes the same two esteros and four taxa, but its full text is unavailable. Do not transfer either estero finding to Pasig River or double-count the apparent research lineage.

A separate 2015 AABE conference abstract by Orozco and Tolentino names Estero de Paco and its tributary Estero de Concordia and reports Gambusia affinis, Rasbora maculata, and Rasbora sp. in both; it gives no collection dates, methods, vouchers, or species-by-station table. Rasbora sp. may overlap the named Rasbora species, and the study is not linked to Orozco/Zafaralla's San Miguel/Quiapo survey lineage. Keep these as historical research-only leads; add no species rows, current-presence, safety, or fishing claims. See national/reviews/ncr-orozco-tolentino-2015-paco-concordia-abstract-review-20261119.json.

DOST-PCIEERD's 2010 report lists an ongoing FEU biodiversity project covering Estero de Paco and Estero de Concordia; the 2011 report lists the Pasig River Stewardship program among completed DOST-GIA projects, and the EMB's NWQSR describes the FEU project's seasonal/temporal biodiversity scope. FEU's 2015 President's Report independently confirms Glorina Orozco's AABE25 presentation in October 2014. These sources do not link the abstract to DOST funding, provide fish tables, or establish a separate survey. No additional species evidence or current claims were added. See national/reviews/ncr-paco-concordia-dost-project-lineage-access-review-20261119.json.

The DENR-NCR 2025 Pasig narrative calls Monopterus albus native, while IUCN's global range also lists the Philippines as native and Philippine NFRDI/DLSU sources describe an introduction (1905 versus first-recorded 1918). Those sources do not resolve taxon concept or Pasig population origin; keep native/introduced status research-only and seek source-linked vouchers and the underlying historical records.

A current-name cross-check confirms the six distinct NMT fish-table binomials are accepted names, but does not validate field identification. The seven-row table repeats Lutjanus argentimaculatus and conflicts with the abstract's six-native/one-invasive count; preserve both original rows and keep all specimen and station assignments research-only.

An official BFAR NCR market report pairs Dendrophysa russelii with Alakaak and includes Navotas in its summary source area; the NFRDI name reference also shows that Alakaak is non-unique. This is market and vernacular-name context, not a river-capture or specimen crosswalk. Keep both NMT Lutjanus rows, the Kabang label, and the species-count conflict unresolved; see national/reviews/ncr-navotas-nmt-vernacular-name-crosscheck-20261119.json.

The directly reviewed PSFS proceedings PDF contains only an aggregate 2018 Marikina abstract: 14 species across five sites, no taxon names or station-by-species table. A 2019 PSFS call invited presenters to submit full papers but does not establish this abstract was published separately. Keep the locality, taxa, and non-native narrative unresolved; seek only a separate manuscript or supplement if authors/PSFS confirm one exists.

The 2011 primary paper confirms BMP001-11 through BMP036-11 and the GenBank db_xref records use BPMP001-11 through BPMP036-11; a bounded public search found no independent museum catalog or supplement to resolve the conflict. The paper names five stations but does not link specimens to them. Keep station, voucher, and taxonomic assignments unresolved; see national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-source-prefix-and-public-catalog-search-20261119.json.

A local screen of five rounded GenBank coordinate clusters against geoBoundaries 2020 ADM3 polygons places four inside Marikina and one in Rodriguez; one lies close to the Marikina-San Mateo boundary. This does not join accessions to the paper's five stations; retain the station and near-boundary assignment as unresolved. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-coarse-municipal-boundary-crosscheck-20261119.json.

Figure 1 names five numbered Marikina-system stations in north-to-south order, which is spatially consistent with the five GenBank coordinate clusters, but supplies no cluster/accession-to-station table. Treat this only as a candidate sequence correspondence; all individual station links remain unverified. See national/reviews/ncr-marikina-2011-figure1-coordinate-cluster-sequence-review-20261119.json.

The official UPLB repository catalogs Glorina D. Perez-Orozco's 2008 estero thesis as an MS Environmental Science thesis, but its full text is unavailable. This conflicts with the DLSU 2008 abstract's PhD wording and does not resolve overlap with the 2012 chapter or station-level fish data. See national/reviews/ncr-orozco-2008-thesis-catalog-access-review-20261119.json.

The 2023 Elsevier fish-microplastics paper is listed as published by PubMed and Ateneo, but a duplicate Ateneo Archium record says withdrawn. Publisher highlights mention Marikina janitor fish, while the accessible abstract does not allocate its scientific-name list by river and the common-name crosswalk is unresolved. Keep it research-only; add no species, occurrence, food-safety, or water-safety rows.

The 2019 Paco/Vitas tilapia biomonitoring paper used juvenile Nile tilapia procured from Cartimar pet market and exposed them in aquaria to water collected from the esteros; the fish are laboratory subjects, not estero captures. A closely matching 2018 DLSU thesis catalog record is unavailable in full text and is not counted as a separate survey. Add no NCR tilapia occurrence or species row from these records; see national/reviews/ncr-paco-vitas-2019-tilapia-biomonitoring-occurrence-exclusion-review-20261119.json.

The EMB-hosted Manila North WRF EPRMP documents three Estero de Vitas freshwater stations, plankton sampling, and macroinvertebrate sampling. The reviewed ecology chapter contains no fish method or taxa; that is a source-coverage limit, not evidence of fish absence. It adds waterbody context only; see national/reviews/ncr-vitas-manila-north-wrf-eprmp-freshwater-fish-scope-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station spacing differs and no coordinate-linked species dataset was found. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

regions.name: Region III (Central Luzon)
openWork: The BMB 2014 Atlas count crosswalk matches the RDP's 168 breakdown at category/count level (153 river systems; 11 lakes, three reservoirs and one swamp), but source lineage, the RDP's separate 202-river statement, all 153 named river systems, current identity and geometry remain unresolved; do not treat this as a verified inventory.

The 70-query CoL XR screen returned one Angat River locality row and 69 bounded zeroes. Follow-up linked it to BPC001-13/ANAd1, source-reported as Arius dispar, while the GBIF Backbone maps the BIN to Netuma thalassina; the BOLD BIN export does not resolve that specimen. A local FAO/HydroRIVERS screen places the source coordinate 0.7 km from an unnamed modeled reach; it is inside a simplified 2020 Bulacan polygon and shares the modeled MAIN_RIV grouping nearest to the GeoNames Angat River point. This supports plausibility only: the GeoNames point is not a route, the reach is unnamed, the exact reach and coordinate uncertainty remain unresolved, and the source chains are not independent. Keep the candidate research-only. The 69 zeroes do not establish absence.

The Pantabangan 2026 journal abstract reports 40 COI sequences/nine species, numerically matching the 2013 GenBank submission's 40 records/nine submitted names; the exact sequence set is unverified. Four earlier Micropterus and two Coptodon GenBank records have Pantabangan locality metadata from 2012, while the abstract calls those two taxa first records. The publisher full text is access-gated and no accession table was found in the bounded search, so retain this as an unresolved crosswalk/first-record conflict. Do not merge the 2013 records, 2026 article, or 2024–2025 student manuscript. See national/reviews/central-luzon-pantabangan-2026-article-access-followup-20261119.json.
Complete separate evidence and coverage results for Pampanga River reaches, Angat and Pantabangan reservoirs, Candaba wetland, tributaries, coast and estuaries.

Publisher-indexed full Silliman Journal text is now queryable and the methods, Nueva Ecija Tables 1-3, and Paitan discussion were re-reviewed. It supports two historical Paitan candidates: Leiopotherapon plumbeus (explicitly named in discussion) and Oreochromis niloticus (a non-empty Paitan Lake cell in Table 3); no additional fish is assigned from flattened rows. Both names are valid in the 2026 Catalog of Fishes, but this does not re-identify specimens or establish current presence. Field dates, vouchers, and rights remain unresolved. The separate janitor-fish lead is repeated through related secondary reports with a Pterygoplichthys parotalis / P. pardalis spelling conflict. The original Agasen report was not obtained; NISSAP is genus-level, and the 2009 report does not resolve presence or absence. Chavez et al. (2006) sampled five Laguna de Bay-basin sites but not Paitan. Do not create species assertions or absence claims. Vaca remains a separate unresolved reservoir: the 2021 joint stocking counts are unallocated, and PIDS provides historical downstream water-quality context but no fish inventory. See national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-silliman-indexed-text-refresh-20261119.json, national/reviews/central-luzon-vaca-water-quality-and-fish-source-gap-20261119.json, national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-historical-fish-name-crosscheck-20261119.json, and national/reviews/central-luzon-paitan-janitor-fish-source-conflict-followup-20261119.json.

The refreshed 2020 Candaba source reports one representative specimen per species group deposited at PSAU, but no accession numbers, field dates, site matrix, or item-specific reuse license; keep it research-only pending independent checks.

The UPLB-provided 1988 Habito thesis abstract reports eight freshwater fish species in eight families from a June–October 1987 survey but provides no fish species names. The official UPLB record says the document is unavailable online and identifies a physical UPLB Main Library Special Collections holding, call number LG 995 1988 Z62 H33. Current access and reproduction rules are unknown; no taxa or maps were extracted. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-habito-1988-thesis-access-review-20261119.json.

Garcia (2010) publisher abstract reports 21 fish species caught in Candaba wetland during 2007–2008 and length-weight relationships for 18 species across 14 families, but no individual names. Direct Wiley full-text retrieval returned 403/timeouts and the bounded exact-title/DOI search found no clearly author-hosted copy. Treat this as an aggregate historical lead; no taxa or app rows were added. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-garcia-2010-fulltext-access-review-20261119.json.

The 2020 publisher paper cites a Bautista & Barila Candaba fish-inventory thesis as 2013 in the introduction and 2003 in the bibliography; the cited title also prints 'Swamo'. A bounded exact-title/author and PSAU/Pampanga Agricultural College search found no independent catalog record or copy. This does not establish that none exists. Keep it as a year-conflicted bibliographic lead only; no thesis species data, app rows, or reuse rights were verified. See national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-bautista-barila-citation-review-20261119.json.

Santos et al. (2010) reports 844 Leiopotherapon plumbeus specimens aggregated across seven localities. Its ResearchGate author-uploaded text describes Maasin River as a Pampanga tributary in Barangay San Agustin, Candaba, and calls the population native; a Maasin-specific sample count, date, voucher, or item reuse license remains unverified. ResearchGate warns the upload may be copyrighted. Keep as a historical research lead; see national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-silver-perch-review-20261119.json and national/reviews/central-luzon-candaba-2010-maasin-rg-fulltext-followup-20261119.json.

The 2019 Bagac conference paper is now identified and its 17/5 totals match the goby synthesis. Keep it separate from the 2022 15-taxon survey and later three-river surveys until field dates, possible sample overlap, and reuse are resolved.

The 2024 Angat ASH abstract names five fish and broad gut-content categories, but has no dated fish-to-site matrix, voucher crosswalk, quantitative prey rows, or item-specific reuse license; retain as research-only and seek an author-hosted full paper or data supplement.

The 19 November National Museum crosswalk shows that the 524-row OBIS refresh mirrors the same GBIF occurrence records; do not count it as an independent L3 species batch. It does not resolve capture waters or other shared-bay sources. Keep Manila Bay shared with L1/L2 and Bataan, Zambales, and Aurora coastal scopes distinct; see national/reviews/manila-bay-national-museum-gbif-obis-crosswalk-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental otter-trawl survey reports a historical top-50 fish-and-invertebrate table grouped by broad Manila Bay sectors including Cavite and Metro Manila. It has no digital haul-coordinate table; the table was not transcribed, and the sectors are not municipality or legal-water boundaries. Keep this shared marine evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-trawl-sector-catch-scope-review-20261119.json.

The 2018 NAST Manila Bay fish-landing abstract reports 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa from 16 landing sites (2012–2015), but gives no site-by-site table or capture-origin records. Its dates and three shared authors overlap the NFRDI 2014–2015 experimental-trawl paper, but the sampling frames differ and a data/program lineage is unconfirmed. Do not add the totals or infer sector-level presence; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2018-nast-manila-bay-landing-trawl-lineage-review-20261119.json.

The NFRDI 2012–2015 ichthyoplankton paper reports 3,008 fish larvae across 34 families; the separate NAST abstract reports 860 larvae across 28 families for 2017. Both describe eight stations and share three authors, but station spacing differs and no coordinate-linked species dataset was found. Keep the windows separate and family-level evidence research-only; see national/reviews/nfrdi-2017-manila-bay-ichthyoplankton-source-screen-20261119.json.

regions.name: Region I (Ilocos Region)
openWork: Build the region's waterbody manifest across Lower Agno, Abra, tributaries, Lingayen Gulf, coast and estuaries.
Keep Dantis and Lacap's five-station 2018 Agno macrofauna source research-only until its locality and table/taxonomy conflicts are resolved; the goby synthesis row is a bibliography lead only.

The Bayaoas River BSRIP 2019/2020 EIS drafts describe one historical five-station freshwater survey, but their fish narrative conflicts with the table and reuse terms are unverified; keep it research-only and do not double-count the draft versions. See national/reviews/region01-bayaoas-river-bsrip-eis-fish-source-screen-20261119.json.

The 2023 Binday Dam paper reports two fish-study locations (Colisao upstream and Aramal downstream) but not numeric fish counts; name/origin claims conflict and its publisher page lists both CC BY-NC 4.0 and CC BY 4.0. Keep it research-only pending taxon and reuse review. See national/reviews/region01-binday-dam-soriano-fish-source-review-20261119.json.

Rojas (2023) reports a three-station Govantes River FAD assessment in Vigan, with 20 claimed macrofauna taxa but 19 Figure 1 caption labels; table cells, exact sampling dates, voucher links and extracted-data reuse terms remain unresolved. Keep it research-only; see national/reviews/region01-govantes-river-rojas-macrofauna-source-screen-20261119.json.

Gaerlan et al. (2018) summarize 2009–2013 small-pelagic fishery landings from ten Lingayen Gulf landing sites and list 20 dominant source labels, but publish no species-by-landing/capture-site matrix; current journal license pages conflict for this 2018 paper. Keep it research-only; see national/reviews/region01-lingayen-small-pelagic-gaerlan-2009-2013-source-review-20261119.json.

The MMSU catalog abstract for Mapalo and Rigua's 2021 Oaig-Upay-Abulao River thesis reports 14 taxa and names three fish, but the 66-leaf thesis is marked Room Use Only and no full checklist, station crosswalk or reuse terms are available. Keep this as an access-limited research lead; see national/reviews/region01-oaig-upay-abulao-mmsu-thesis-catalog-access-review-20261119.json.

For Paoay Lake, Aquino et al. (2008) provide a zooplankton survey and only PAMB-personal-communication fish labels, while Magistrado et al. (2026) provide non-indigenous-species risk categories rather than a new fish survey. Keep both as research-only leads; see national/reviews/region01-paoay-lake-fish-evidence-screen-20261119.json.

The 2026 Maluyo River article reports 16 fauna rows, but its methods do not identify actual fish sampling effort, dates, station assignments or vouchers; its fish labels include mixed taxonomic resolution and the publisher page has conflicting license statements. Keep research-only; see national/reviews/region01-maluyo-river-fauna-source-screen-20261119.json.

The DMMMSU repository exposes only an abstract for a 2021 transplanted-mangrove fish study in La Union. It reports aggregate counts at three unnamed stations and the unresolved spelling Salotherodon melanotheron; no full fish list, method or license was verified. Keep this as an abstract-only lead; see national/reviews/region01-la-union-transplanted-mangrove-thesis-abstract-screen-20261119.json.

The PSA Region I 2024 Municipal Fisheries Situationer reports provincial marine and inland production and top common/local catch labels, including Mullet (Kapak) and Freshwater Goby (Biya). It names no waterbody or source site and gives no scientific names or vouchers; production is not occurrence or abundance evidence. Use only to prioritize distinct inland and marine source searches; see national/reviews/region01-la-union-psa-municipal-fisheries-2024-source-screen-20261119.json.

Balneg et al. (2025) provide a dated Caba bottom-set-gillnet catch study across four barangays/eight fishing spots. Its 43 table labels include a crab and Mugil sp.; the catch tables are site-aggregated, voucher IDs are absent, several names/statistics conflict internally, effort wording is unresolved, and no article license was verified. A separate authoritative catalog crosscheck suggests name-string variants but does not identify sampled specimens; keep research-only pending taxon, voucher, effort, site-crosswalk and rights checks.
